title: Omnicommerce website

hero.about: Omnicommerce connects point of sale, eCommerce, delivery, inventory, loyalty and workforce in one AI-powered platform for modern retail, from the register to the doorstep. I designed the marketing website: the page system, navigation, product UI mocks and the visual language that holds fifteen pages together.

Omnicommerce connects point of sale, eCommerce, delivery, inventory, loyalty and workforce in one AI-powered platform for modern retail, from the register to the doorstep. I designed the marketing website: the page system, navigation, product UI mocks and the visual language that holds fifteen pages together.
modules.alt: Hero for the Omnicommerce website case study: the headline “Omnicommerce is the unified OS for modern retail” above a desktop monitor showing the new home page, with the project meta and an About paragraph.

modules.name: 02 Overview
heading: A product with
ten modules and
one story to tell
modules.lede: Make ten modules feel simple, prove the product is real, and lead every visitor to one action.
text:
Product & brand designer
Website, end to end
Make ten modules feel simple, prove the product is real, and lead every visitor to one action.
modules.alt: Project overview listing client, industry, role and tools, with the goal of making ten modules feel simple, and scope chips for 15 pages, 3 mega menus, 8 product mocks and 92 icons.

modules.name: 03 Process
heading: Thoughtful
process shaping
a clear first visit
text: Group ten modules into four pillars operators already think in
Design the menus first: with this many modules, the menu is the overview
Build a section library before any page
Draw product UI mocks from the real modules
One call to action on every page: schedule a demo
modules.alt: Five-step design process: Map, Navigate, System, Prove and Convert, each with a one-line description.

modules.name: 04 Problem
heading: Nine tools.
Nine logins.
No shared data.
modules.lede: Operators in this market run one tool for the register, one for online orders, one for delivery, one for loyalty and one for compliance. Stock oversells, purchase limits slip and reporting is manual. The site had to name that pain before it sold anything.
text: Operators in this market run one tool for the register, one for online orders, one for delivery, one for loyalty and one for compliance. Stock oversells, purchase limits slip and reporting is manual. The site had to name that pain before it sold anything.
9 logins, nine invoices, nine vendors to manage
Inventory reconciled by hand, every night
One customer looks like three strangers across store, web and app
Compliance reports assembled from manual exports
One login, one invoice, one source of truth
Stock syncs across registers, web and warehouse in real time
Every purchase builds one universal customer profile
Compliance reporting runs in the background, audit-ready
The stack toggle from the home page: one click swaps the broken tools for the connected platform.
modules.alt: The home page stack toggle in both states: a disconnected stack of nine tools, and the connected Omnicommerce network where every module is linked.

modules.name: 05 Audit: previous site
heading: The old site
said a lot and
showed very little
modules.lede: The previous Omnicommerce website was one long page. Before designing anything new, I audited it against the questions a retail operator asks on a first visit: what does it do, is it for me, can I trust it, what do I do next.
text: The previous Omnicommerce website was one long page. Before designing anything new, I audited it against the questions a retail operator asks on a first visit: what does it do, is it for me, can I trust it, what do I do next.
A logo and one Contact button. Ten modules and no way to explore them.
“Take your operations to next level” could describe any software.
Point of sale, loyalty, marketing and compliance never appear by name.
Clothing racks and warehouses where the product UI should be.
Real screens, shrunk into devices until nothing is legible.
“Connect for demo” in the hero, “Contact us” everywhere else.
No SOC 2, PCI DSS or Metrc in a regulated industry.
“Each Modules has been designed”, “Our app suite encompass”.
modules.alt: Annotated audit of the previous one-page Omnicommerce website, with eight numbered issues from no navigation and stock photos to missing trust signals and copy slips.

modules.name: 06 Problem and solution
heading: Solving real
problems with
a simpler story
text: Ten modules read as complicated enterprise software.
Buyers don’t trust software they can’t see.
A regulated industry, where trust decides the shortlist.
Four pillars and a mega menu that works as the product map.
Eight product UI mocks instead of stock imagery, on every page.
SOC 2, PCI DSS and Metrc up front, and one action: schedule a demo.
modules.alt: Three problems paired with three solutions: four pillars and a mega menu, eight product UI mocks instead of stock imagery, and trust badges with one action to schedule a demo.

modules.name: 07 Audience
heading: Built for
operators who
run everything
text: Checkout with purchase limits, loyalty and compliance at every register.
Routing, dispatch, live ETAs and delivery-window tracking from one map.
Bins, FEFO picking, transfers and lab results across every warehouse.
modules.alt: Three audience cards: dispensaries, delivery fleets and distributors, each with the jobs the platform does for them.

modules.name: 08 Site map
heading: Structured
site map for
fast decisions
modules.alt: Site map of the new website: Home branching into Products, Solutions, Resources and Company, with every page listed under its section.

modules.name: 09 Navigation
heading: The menu is
the product map,
not a list of links
text: See how every module talks to every other one.
Live stock synced to every register
Four pillars, four columns. Grouping cuts how many choices a visitor scans at once (Hick’s law).
A benefit under every item. “Live stock synced to every register” says more than “Inventory”.
A tour card in every menu. It ties the modules back into one platform, and follows a pattern buyers know from other SaaS sites (Jakob’s law).
Run every store like your best one.
We're with you after go-live, too.
modules.alt: The three mega menus (Products, Solutions and Resources), each with a benefit line under every item and a tour card, plus notes on Hick’s law and Jakob’s law.

modules.name: 10 Typography
heading: Consistent
visual system for
a growing product
text: Headlines. Bold 86 / 84, SemiBold 50, 22, 17. Tight tracking for a confident, compact voice.
Body, UI and labels. Regular 20 / 32 lead, 16 / 26 body, SemiBold 16 buttons, 12.5 caps eyebrows.
Compliance that runs in the background.
From first click to front door.
Fast, compliant checkout with purchase limits, loyalty and AI upsells built in, so budtenders can focus on the guest.
modules.alt: Typography for the website: Bricolage Grotesque for headlines and Figtree for body and UI, with a type scale from Hero 86 down to the eyebrow label.

modules.name: 11 Colour and depth
heading: Colours
text: Background blur 22, soft drop shadow. Nav bar, cards, menus.
Resting surfaces: feature cards, chips, inputs.
Raised surfaces: product mocks, demo form, footer.
modules.alt: Colour palette of ten named tokens from Blue and Navy to Leaf, Mint and Amber with hex values, and the glass and two shadow levels used for depth.

modules.name: 12 Iconography
heading: 92 icons,
one stroke,
one grid
modules.lede: A single outline family on a 24 px grid, drawn for every module, menu item and feature card, so a new page never waits on new icons.
text: A single outline family on a 24 px grid, drawn for every module, menu item and feature card, so a new page never waits on new icons.
92 icons, each a component in the Omnicommerce file.
modules.alt: Grid of the 92 outline icons drawn on a 24 px grid, each a component in the Omnicommerce file.

modules.name: 13 Section library
heading: One library,
fifteen pages,
zero one-offs
modules.lede: Every page is assembled from the same sections. Product pages share one rhythm, and a new module page needs no new design.
text: Every page is assembled from the same sections. Product pages share one rhythm, and a new module page needs no new design.
modules.alt: The section library: page hero, feature grid, FAQ, split feature with stat, footer and CTA band, the sections every page is assembled from.

modules.name: 14 Interactive components
heading: Show the
stack problem,
then the fix
modules.lede: The hero is a live network. Toggle “Your stack today” and the modules break apart into nine disconnected tools; toggle back and they reconnect around one source of truth.
text: The hero is a live network. Toggle “Your stack today” and the modules break apart into nine disconnected tools; toggle back and they reconnect around one source of truth.
Platform tabs walk every module with a live mock, one click each.
Point of Sale, eCommerce, Delivery, Marketing, Intelligence and Inventory share one layout: headline, three proof points, a link and the module’s UI.
modules.alt: The interactive hero network in both toggle states, and the platform tabs that walk every module with a live mock.

everywhere,
for every visitor

text: “Schedule a demo” is the primary button in the header, the hero, every page CTA and the footer, with “Talk to sales” as the quiet second path. The demo page is a short form and nothing else.
A 30-minute walkthrough tailored to your stores, fleet and goals, with no generic slideware.
Full platform demo tailored to your operation
No contract required for the pilot program
